chunks.content: ## Overview of Asymmetric Segmented Shoulder Design This section explains the design concept of an asymmetrical, split, and foldable shoulder model. Key elements include the disappearance and transfer of traditional neckline lines (A-neckline, Xiu Long-neckline, B-neckline) to new positions such as the shoulder split line, reflecting the asymmetrical style. The section sets the foundation for the pattern drafting process. --- ## Pattern Drafting for Asymmetrical Shoulder Design This section covers the step-by-step process of drafting the asymmetrical shoulder pattern using digital tools, emphasizing unlocking symmetry constraints and creating division lines. - The original symmetrical front circle is unlocked to allow asymmetrical editing. - A division line is drawn according to the style, typically 4 cm from a reference point. - Cutting lines, which are complex with multiple bends, are drawn separately using traditional methods. - Folds are positioned away from the BP (bust point) to avoid incomplete closure and to maintain integration. - Fold positions can be adjusted and duplicated (using Ctrl-C, Ctrl-V) for desired placement. - Fold lengths are modified to control decorative effects; longer folds shorten the timespan of the fold effect. - The original left A position is relocated, and the sleeve is divided into segments to form folds, bringing the style closer to the desired design. --- ## Sleeve and Fold Adjustment Procedures This section details the steps for adjusting folds and sleeve measurements to ensure proper fit and style coherence. - Copying and rotating lines to align sleeve parts with the BP point. - Measuring sleeve length precisely (e.g., 18.1 cm diameter). - Adding points along the hand edge and creating straight lines for clean sleeve edges. - Uniform adjustment of fold positions to bring fold points closer or redistribute folds evenly. - Addition of cutting lines to finalize upper shoulder segmentation. --- ## Neckline and Shoulder Rotation Techniques This section explains how to cut and rotate neckline and shoulder segments, maintaining key construction principles. - The upper shoulder is cut, followed by the neckline, which maintains the original round shape. - Rotation is performed while keeping the front and center lines fixed. - Since folds eliminate the neckline point, it is pushed to the cutting line for accuracy. - Neckline edge lengths are adjusted uniformly (e.g., 118.3 cm) to maintain symmetry after rotation. - Use of mouse and right-click actions to scan and position small pattern pieces precisely. - Transfer of shoulder "speakers" (pattern extensions) with rotation around the front center line. - Deletion of auxiliary lines after completing transfers for clarity. --- ## Speaker Rotation and Length Adjustment This section focuses on detailed manipulation of shoulder pattern extensions ("speakers") to fit the asymmetrical design. - Speakers on both sides are rotated and positioned to ensure equal length (e.g., 118.3 cm). - Adjustments consider student feedback regarding changes at the neckline top and bottom due to folds. - Points on speakers are pushed toward segment lines to maintain design integrity.

chunks.content: - Deletion of auxiliary lines after completing transfers for clarity. --- ## Speaker Rotation and Length Adjustment This section focuses on detailed manipulation of shoulder pattern extensions ("speakers") to fit the asymmetrical design. - Speakers on both sides are rotated and positioned to ensure equal length (e.g., 118.3 cm). - Adjustments consider student feedback regarding changes at the neckline top and bottom due to folds. - Points on speakers are pushed toward segment lines to maintain design integrity. - Volume and length adjustments of speakers use right-click functions and precise measurement inputs (e.g., 38.1 cm). - Rotation and merging of voice points (pivot points) ensure smooth transitions between pattern segments. --- ## Original Order and Curve Editing in Pattern Drafting This section clarifies the correction of pattern point orders and curve adjustments for a clean final pattern. - Deletion of extra points to avoid distortion in the original order of the pattern. - Use of editor tools to convert unnecessary points into free curve points, smoothing the pattern outline. - Removal of extra lines created during speaker rotation to maintain pattern clarity. - Adjusting the original order ensures angles (e.g., 90 degrees at the back) and segment lines remain precise. --- ## Final Pattern Boxing and 3D Visualization This section discusses preparing the pattern for 3D modeling and final adjustments. - Deletion of default box lines generated during voice rotation to avoid clutter. - Boxing of key pattern lines (segment line, keyline, side box) is done separately due to asymmetry. - Use of a 3D window to preview the pattern volume and fit. - Large volume changes from rotation are fine-tuned by appropriate rotation adjustments. - Particular attention is given to small shoulder segment lines that may stretch during adjustment, requiring manual correction to reach 100% accuracy. - Final unharden (softening) of pattern lines ensures proper flexibility and fit. --- # Terminology and Tools - **A-neckline, Xiu Long-neckline, B-neckline:** Traditional neckline styles referenced and repositioned in the asymmetrical design. - **BP Point:** Bust point, a key reference in pattern drafting. - **Speaker:** Pattern extension pieces at shoulders used for folds and shaping. - **Ctrl-C, Ctrl-V:** Copy and paste functions for duplicating pattern elements. - **Rotation and Voice Points:** Techniques to pivot and adjust segments around fixed points. - **Boxing:** Creating a bounding box around pattern segments for 3D modeling. - **Unharden:** Softening or releasing constraints on pattern lines for flexibility. --- This document provides a detailed technical guide on designing and drafting an asymmetrical segmented shoulder pattern, including fold placement, rotation techniques, and final pattern preparation for manufacturing or 3D visualization.
